headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can egress broadly, but LlamaFactory is local-only with no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces, so pairwise interaction risks are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory exposes no clipboard, filesystem, stdin/stdout, or MCP bridge, so there is no documented channel for Airflow output to be ingested as instructions by default. The pairwise pathway is therefore provably blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Airflow output into LlamaFactory input, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared queues and shared folders.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes, shared workspace access, or authenticated sharing. Airflow touches no declared data classes here, and LlamaFactory has no filesystem read or network egress, so there is no plausible leakage path in the current pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later pointed at PHI, secrets, or customer records, reassess leakage risk.
IF a shared workspace is mounted, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace.
Keep sensitive datasets out of both agents.
Review any future data-class changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource shown, there is no capability conflict in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF shared OAuth scopes or a mutable database are introduced, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only in this deployment.
Avoid giving both agents access to the same mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can produce automation outputs, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking authority and no stdin/stdout or file ingestion surface. That makes a default cascade from Airflow into LlamaFactory unlikely; any harmful chain would require an unusual external bridge.
conditions: IF an operator feeds Airflow-generated text into LlamaFactory as authoritative input, cascading error risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped in a downstream action pipeline, reassess severity.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing Airflow outputs.
Do not auto-feed Airflow artifacts into LlamaFactory prompts.
Add a verification step if a downstream pipeline is later built.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to score. Because the profiles are silent, the other agent is not separately cited beyond the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced, reassess residency and retention.
IF either agent is deployed under a specific compliance regime, compare policies before use.
mitigations: Check retention settings if regulated data is added.
requires-engineering: map both agents to the target compliance regime.
